value_updates.allocation_trigger: successful mint without a referral code

verdicts.decision_note: The source establishes random existing-holder allocation for no-referral mints but does not establish that this path issued both Small- and Big-Block tickets.
Removing Big Blocks leaves the no-referral allocation path with the Small Block prize ticket only.
The client explicitly leaves the first-mint ticket recipient rule unresolved because no earlier NFT exists.
The required popup behavior establishes random ticket allocation when the referral code is absent or invalid.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports the contract's concrete no-ticket behavior for the first-mint edge case.
First concrete failure of the standard no-referral path: a completed USDC purchase generated no randomly allocated ticket.
The client materially reopens whether a no-referral purchase must generate a ticket.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports that no-referral mints now generate a ticket.

verdicts.decision_note: Target-specific post-failure implementation claim; the edit removes the unsupported assertion that this source explicitly identifies the ticket's random recipient.
The source reports that randomly issued tickets are not registering in totals, which concerns ticket accounting rather than changing the recipient-allocation rule.
The client explicitly requires one ticket for a standard no-referral primary mint and random assignment to an existing holder.
The proposed first-mint exception conflicts with the client's preceding one-ticket-per-mint rule and requires client resolution.
The client unambiguously accepts the executable exception that mint number one receives no ticket when no earlier NFT exists.
The client accepts the concrete backend rule that processRandomReferral credits the randomly selected token with one ticket.
The leaderboard total only suggests that a ticket was issued somewhere; the client cannot identify the recipient, so the evidence does not verify random allocation to an existing NFT holder.

missing_event_candidates.description: The client reports that randomly issued tickets do not appear in the recorded totals, indicating an accounting or registration failure rather than a recipient-allocation change.
